Nyircsaszari Jewish Cemetery One

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírcsászári, Hungary

Not demolished. Nyírcsászári's Jewish cemetery appears on an 1893 cadastral map, its earliest documented reference, though none of its surviving gravestones have legible dates. The village had 26 Jewish residents out of 424 in 1880, a number that fluctuated over the following decades - 74 in 1910, down to 45 by 1930 and 25 by 1941. Locally prominent Jewish residents included landowner Jenő Blau, his son Dezső (a crop trader who opened a bakery in 1918), and Antal Reinitz, a farmer with rabbinical training who served for years as village representative. In 1944, Nyírcsászári's Jews were gathered and deported to Auschwitz; by 1945 none remained in the village.
